diagnosis.root_cause: Evening shared-bandwidth congestion on EPON0/7: the PON is carrying near-peak traffic while the subscriber's optical path, ONU, authentication, VLAN, router, and OLT are healthy.
evidence: The complaint is time-specific: service is acceptable during the day and slows every evening, which is consistent with busy-period contention.
The subscriber's RX power is -21.27 dBm and TX power is 2.37 dBm, both within the normal EPON ranges.
Seven-day RX variation is narrow and remains in the normal band; TX power and bias current are also stable, ruling out fibre degradation and laser degradation.
Distance remains constant at 167, ruling out a fibre-path change.
All probed peers on EPON0/7 are online and responding, so there is no ONU, splitter, or port outage.
The OLT responds to ping, SNMP, and subtree queries, with healthy CPU, memory, and temperature; the router heartbeat is also healthy.
The subscriber has only 2 sessions in 24 hours with approximately normal session duration, so this is not session flapping or an authentication fault.
RADIUS records are present and consistent, and the expected customer VLAN 1017 is active.
EPON0/7 traffic is currently 912 Mbps with a 948 Mbps peak versus a 488 Mbps average, indicating the shared PON is approaching its practical capacity during busy periods.
Because the traffic symptom is shared on the PON and the direct port view contains healthy surviving ONUs, the appropriate scope is pon_port rather than single_customer or OLT.

remediation.action: Review EPON0/7 utilization and per-ONU traffic during the evening peak, apply or verify fair-use/QoS scheduling, and reduce oversubscription by moving customers to another PON or upgrading/splitting capacity. Continue monitoring peak utilization after the change.

ground_truth.root_cause: EPON0/7 carries 47 customers and its evening load is reaching 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average, close to the port's shared capacity ceiling. Throughput degrades for everyone on the port during peak hours. No optical or authentication fault exists.
expected_reasoning: The complaint is time-of-day specific, which points at load rather than at a physical fault
RX is flat at -21.2 dBm inside the noise floor, and TX, bias, voltage and distance are all stable
The live probe shows every ONU on the port online with normal optical readings
RADIUS is clean and sessions are long and stable, so authentication is not involved
PON port traffic is at 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average
Daily traffic for this customer is roughly three times the network mean and rising, not falling
Every fault-driven degradation reduces traffic; congestion raises it, so the direction is the discriminator
The customer's own throughput series drops sharply during the same evening hours each day
The port carries 47 customers, at the top of the observed occupancy distribution
This is capacity exhaustion on a shared port, not a fault on any one line

expected_escalation.review_reason: EPON0/7 needs a capacity review; 47 customers on one port with evening load near ceiling

distractors: Multi-customer slowness resembles a splitter or feeder degradation
Elevated OLT CPU and temperature could be read as device stress causing the slowness
Reduced throughput in the speed series looks like a link problem
